## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Visuddhimagga nidānakathā* ("An Introduction to the Visuddhimagga") is an introductory text accompanying Buddhaghosa's *Visuddhimagga*, preserved in the Anya (miscellaneous) section of the Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana collection [Catalog; Wen]. Bibliographic tables associate the composition or publication of the text with modern Burmese monastic scholarship linked to the Sixth Buddhist Council (Chaṭṭha Saṅgīti) and Mahāsi Sayādaw [Nyanatusita 2008; Wen]. In modern research, the treatise has also been examined for lexical and ritual developments in late Pali literature, such as occurrences of devotional terminology like *buddhapūjā* [Sugunasiri 2012].

 However, DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse, calculating 2,921 shared passages across 106 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most prominent alignments occur with the classical commentary literature (*aṭṭhakathā*), notably the *Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā* (121 matches), the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* (67 matches), the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā* (71 matches), and the *Dīghanikāye Sīlakkhandhavaggaṭṭhakathā* (80 matches) [DharmaNexus]. It also shares significant material with both volumes of the *Visuddhimagga* itself, the *Mahāvaṃsa*, and Vinaya sub-commentaries such as the *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā* and *Vimativinodanī-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
